newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury ups stakes on food hygiene.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury ups stakes on food hygiene.

text.p: British food retailer J.Sainsbury Plc on Wednesday unveiled a new range of bacteria-fighting products aimed to address growing public concern over food hygiene.
The supermarket group is launching the UK's first range of kitchen and household products, impregnated with Microban, an anti-bacterial agent, developed by U.S. firm Microban Products Company.
Sainsbury has signed a two-year exclusivity agreement for food related products with Microban International, which has the distribution rights to Microban.

The initial range of some 60 products -- including chopping boards, dish cloths, bin liners and kitchen utensils, will be available by late summer. Sainsbury will incorporate Microban into its own food preparation facilities and hopes suppliers will also introduce it over time.
Sainsbury will spend around 5 million pounds ($8.2 million) on the project in the first year.

Sainsbury marketing director Kevin McCarten said the project had been budgeted for some time. "How much money we put behind it (going forward) depends on how it goes...how successful Microban is," he told journalists,".

The retailer believes Microban will be popular given growing public concern about food safety after a spate of food poising scares in Britain - including an E-coli outbreak in Scotland, which claimed several lives.
"We're confident our customers will like it," McCarten said.
Microban's effectiveness will be certified by LawLabs, a leading UK authority on trading standards and regulatory compliance for consumer products.
Sainsbury is already working with suppliers to try and get them to introduce Microban, but won't make it compulsory. "It's unlikely we demand our suppliers comply," McCarten said.

Microban is effective against a wide range of bacteria, including food poisoning agents such as salmonella and E-coli. Microban's active ingredient - triclosan, made by Ciba-Geigy - works by splitting or rupturing the bacteria's cells.
Sainsbury emphasised however, it would still be necessary to keep utensils clean even if they were impregnated with Microban.
Triclosan has been used for more than 20 years in the UK in products such as soaps, deodorants and more recently mouthwashes and toothpastes.

But Microban has developed a process to incorporate triclosan into a wide range of plastics, so that the protection against bacteria lasts for the life of the product. Microban's effectiveness in plastics is not reduced by washing or wiping.
Independent laboratory tests by Sainsbury have shown that Microban can destroy up to 99.9 percent of bacteria that come into contact with it.

In the United States Microban is already used as an anti-bacterial preservative in surface and flooring products used in hospitals, laboratories and food processing sites as well as consumer products ranging from kitchen wipes to athletic socks.

Microban has also announced an agreement with Marks & Spencer Plc for a range of bath mats and towels impregnated with Microban. Protection is guaranteed for up to 50 washes. The towels will be available at Marks & Spencer stores in Shoreham and Camberley in southern England from May 19, and from other stores in August.
Microban said M&S were currently developing the implementation of Microban technology in a number of other product areas.
Bill Rubinstein, president of Microban International, said these were the firm's first major partnerships outside the United States.
He said Microban would shortly announce new deals in the United States for toothbrushes offering Microban protection. -- London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7717
